panels.title: Energy in (range)
panels.description: Summed from clamped 20-minute increments (cap 400 Wh / 15 Ah per pack per step), so a counter reset cannot spike the chart. Subquery points align to the epoch, which overstates ranges shorter than ~6 h (about +3% at 6 h, +16% at 1 h); use a day or more for exact totals.

panels.title: Round-trip efficiency (range)
panels.description: Bank Wh out / Wh in over the selected range (measured V×I). Only meaningful over ranges that contain whole charge/discharge cycles (a week or more); over a short range it just reflects which half of the cycle you are looking at.

panels.title: Cell voltage envelope — bank min / max
panels.description: Lowest and highest single cell across all online packs. With vendor SOC rejected this is the honest state-of-charge indicator for LTO: knee ≈2.5 V, do not exceed 2.8 V.

panels.title: Cell delta per pack (mV)
panels.description: max−min cell voltage inside each pack. A pack drifting apart here is the usual cause of a current-share skew in the row below.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: Bank-wide cell temperature envelope plus MOS temperature per pack.

panels.title: MOS state per pack
panels.description: 1 = MOSFET closed (conducting). A single pack with its discharge MOS open shows up in the current-share panel as a skew — check here first.

panels.title: Alarms per pack
panels.description: Active alarm flags by type; the 'any' rows are always present so an all-clear still renders. Details per pack: Daly BMS → Alarms.

panels.title: Bank energy (Wh) — measured V×I, summed across packs
Energy per hour (bank Σ, Wh)
panels.description: Bank total energy (sum across packs) integrated from measured power V×I. received=charge (green,up), spent=discharge (orange,down). No freshness gate: a brief telemetry gap won't blank a bar. Reset caveat: sum(increase()) inherits counter-reset artifacts (rare with persistence). Bar granularity is fixed (per hour / 24 h / 30 d) via min-interval; the panel FOLLOWS the dashboard time picker — widen the range to see more bars (a short range leaves the day/month panels near-empty). Summed from clamped 20-minute increments (cap 400 Wh / 15 Ah per pack per step), so a counter reset cannot spike the chart. Buckets are aligned to the Unix epoch (UTC), not to local midnight — read them as rolling 24 h / 30 d bins, not calendar days/months.

panels.title: Packs — snapshot
panels.description: Per-pack snapshot. V / current / share are freshness-gated (<10 min) so a dead pack cannot skew the share denominator; its row still shows via age / Wh / SOC. current-share = pack current / total. vendor SOC shown for reference only — the controller computes it incorrectly, do NOT treat it as ground truth. Summed from clamped 20-minute increments (cap 400 Wh / 15 Ah per pack per step), so a counter reset cannot spike the chart. Subquery points align to the epoch, which overstates ranges shorter than ~6 h (about +3% at 6 h, +16% at 1 h); use a day or more for exact totals.

panels.title: Current share % per pack (under load)
panels.description: Share of total bank current per pack (only shown when |Σcurrent|>2 A; noise-gated at idle).

panels.title: Voltage spread (mV)
panels.description: Measured pack-voltage spread across the bank (max-min). Larger under load = current-sharing/IR mismatch.

panels.title: Data integrity — why the energy numbers can be trusted
Implausible / dropped frames per s
panels.description: Frames rejected before any metric update. A steady implausible_* rate means a pack is emitting garbage registers; the energy panels above exclude those frames.

panels.title: Coulomb samples rejected / state write errors per s
panels.description: Non-zero here means the Wh/Ah counters are diverging from reality: samples dropped/clamped at integration, or the persisted state file failing to write (counter would reset on restart).

panels.title: State file age
panels.description: Seconds since the coulomb/energy state was last durably written. Grows only while the exporter receives no frames or the disk is failing; compare with 'Worst frame age'.

panels.title: Current offset — applied vs estimate
panels.description: What the exporter subtracts from each pack's reported current before feeding the daly_bms_calibrated_* counters, against what the estimator currently believes. They differ while a gate holds the correction — see the Calibration state panel. The raw daly_bms_charge/discharge_* counters are never touched by this.

panels.title: Peer cross-check — relative offset & disagreement
panels.description: Packs in parallel carry the same current, so regressing one pack's reading against a peer's measures the difference of their zero errors directly — with no loss term in it. Disagreement is the gap between that and what the charge balance concluded; it is expected to be non-zero (the balance also absorbs losses the balancer under-reports), so watch the trend, not the value. Crossing calibration_peer_max_disagreement_amperes freezes the correction.

panels.title: Accuracy bound of the estimate
panels.description: Cap / window: the worst the BMS's own (bounded) state of charge can still be skewing the estimate. The correction stays held until this drops below calibration_max_anchor_error_amperes, so this panel is the warmup progress bar — it falls as 1/window.

panels.title: Calibration state
panels.description: Why the correction is or is not being applied. 'warmup' is the normal state for the first ~33 days on a 40 Ah pack; 'peer disagreement' means the parallel packs and the charge balance stopped telling the same story and the offset has been frozen at its last good value.

panels.title: Balancer bleed per 24 h (Ah)
panels.description: Charge the passive balancer burns in its resistors. It enters through the current sensor and never comes back out, so it is a real part of the gap between energy in and energy out — in production 9–14% of throughput, which is most of what the raw counters showed as 'losses'.

panels.title: Energy per 24 h — raw vs calibrated (bank Σ, Wh)
panels.description: The payoff panel. While the correction is held the two pairs sit on top of each other; once it engages, the calibrated pair is the one whose books balance.

panels.title: Round-trip efficiency, calibrated (range)
panels.description: The same figure as the headline efficiency stat, but computed from the calibrated counters. Over a range holding whole cycles the remaining gap should be the balancer bleed plus the ~1.5% charge/discharge voltage difference — not a sensor that cannot find zero.
